faq.a: A rule is an agreement about how people in a group should act, like no hands in football or wait your turn to speak. Rules help everyone know what to expect.

faq.q: What happens when there are no rules?
faq.a: Without rules, people expect different things, so it is confusing and unfair. The strongest or loudest may get their way, and arguments start.
asks: Why does a game need rules?

faq.q: Why do people argue without rules?
faq.a: Each person thinks their own way is right. With no shared agreement, there is no fair way to decide, so people start shouting instead.
asks: Why do fights start in games?

faq.a: Rules can be made by the group itself, like friends agreeing on a game, or by people chosen to lead, like a school council or a government. Rules feel fairer when the people who follow them have a say.
Good rules keep things fair and safe for everyone, not just the strong. But a rule can be unfair too, and then people can talk about changing it in a fair, peaceful way.

facts: Laws are rules made for a whole country by its government or parliament.
Football's first shared rulebook was written in London in 1863, because schools played with different rules.
